title: Cyrus and the Playlist
premise: Ada Okonkwo has spent seventeen years perfecting the art of being fine in Millbrook, a town of nine hundred where she is the only out kid. When her AP English teacher assigns a college essay prompt that demands one honest answer, Ada writes about Cyrus, the boy who left town two years ago and whose mixtape still lives on her phone — and accidentally submits it to a statewide contest that publishes every entry online. As the essay goes viral in all the wrong ways, Ada must lead her underdog quiz bowl team to a championship nobody cares about while fighting for the one that does: the right to tell her own story before someone else tells it for her. She wins neither trophy cleanly, but she finally answers the question honestly — to the whole town, and to Cyrus himself.
about_author: Casper Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town debate coach who grew up as the only queer kid in a farming county of eleven hundred people. They write stories about loud hearts in quiet places.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Fine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Millbrook through Ada's meticulously maintained 'fine' — the jokes, the deflections, the playlist she curates like armor. Her best friend Dee calls out the performance; Ada deflects again. Beat: establish the mask and its cost.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mr. Vasquez assigns the college essay: answer one honest question you can't stop answering. That night Ada opens a blank document and types 'Cyrus' before deleting it at 2 a.m. Beat: the crack in the dam.

chapters.title: Mixtape Archaeology
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback-tinged. She replays the playlist Cyrus made her before he moved away — twenty-two songs, each a thing he never said aloud. Dee catches her listening and asks the real question. Beat: grief disguised as nostalgia.

chapters.title: Quiz Bowl Is Not a Metaphor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Coach Brandt recruits Ada to captain the dying quiz bowl team; the state tournament is eight weeks out. She joins for the transcript line, insisting it means nothing. Beat: reluctant commitment, comic team assembly.

chapters.title: The Accidental Submit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Racing a deadline, she pastes the raw, unguarded draft — the one about Cyrus — into the statewide contest portal meant for polished essays. Confirmation email: received. Beat: horror, denial, refresh-refresh-refresh.

chapters.title: Published Means Public
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. The contest site posts all entries. Dee reads Ada's essay at 7 a.m., then watches it spread through the school group chats. She must decide whether to warn Ada or let truth arrive on its own schedule. Beat: loyalty vs. protection.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Screenshot
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The essay reaches Millbrook. A classmate's mom posts it to the town Facebook page with a prayer-hands emoji. Ada walks the halls feeling read, labeled, exposed. Beat: public shaming begins; the mask shatters publicly.

chapters.title: Coach Brandt's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The school board suggests Ada step down as captain until things 'cool off.' Brandt refuses quietly, giving Ada a choice framed as a choice. Beat: first adult ally; duty vs. self-preservation.

chapters.title: Practice Round, Real Stakes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ragtag team — anxious Priya, stoner-genius Marcus, silent freshman Theo — pulls an upset at a scrimmage. For ninety minutes Ada forgets the internet exists. Beat: found-team joy, brief reprieve.

chapters.title: Cyrus Replies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A DM from Cyrus: 'Is this about me?' Two years of silence, now a blinking cursor. Their exchange is guarded, funny, devastating. He says he's coming home for Thanksgiving. Beat: hope and terror entwined.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Regional quiz bowl quarterfinals. The team wins ugly while half the gym films Ada instead of the match. Marcus rages at the injustice; Ada thanks him anyway. Beat: rising tension, the crowd as antagonist.

chapters.title: Thanksgiving Traffic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cyrus comes back. They meet at the gas station where everything used to happen; the conversation is all subtext and old songs. He apologizes without explaining. Beat: love rekindled but untrusted.

chapters.title: What Duty Sounds Like
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV (interlude). Why he left: his father's church, his own cowardice, the promise to be 'normal' until college. He reads Ada's published essay twice and recognizes the boy he failed to be. Beat: antagonist-of-self revealed sympathetically.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Fallout
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Semifinal victory, but a rival school circulates Ada's essay as trash-talk material. Theo, the silent freshman, stands up in the parking lot and says his first full sentence of the book: 'Leave her alone.' Beat: loyalty crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The school board votes on whether Ada can compete at state. Dee speaks, Brandt speaks, and finally Ada speaks — not fine, not funny, just true. The vote passes narrowly. Beat: midpoint climax of the public arc.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Songs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finally asks Cyrus what the playlist meant. He admits track fourteen was a confession she never decoded. They almost kiss; he flinches at a passing car. Beat: intimacy blocked by inherited fear.

chapters.title: State Finals Eve
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The night before finals: study session that becomes a vigil. Each teammate confesses why they're really here. Ada admits she doesn't care about the trophy anymore — she cares about finishing something honestly. Beat: emotional convergence.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the state final, mid-match, a moderator reads a toss-up that is essentially the essay prompt. Ada buzzes in and answers it — about Cyrus, about herself — on stage, live-streamed. Millbrook watches. Beat: CLIMAX; truth spoken at full volume.

chapters.title: Winning Ugly
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Distracted by her own courage, Ada misses the final question; the team loses by ten points. But the room gives them a standing ovation, and the clip outruns the shame. Beat: losing the championship that didn't matter.

chapters.title: Track Fourteen
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Outside the auditorium, Cyrus plays track fourteen from his phone, out loud, in front of everyone leaving the building. It's a love song, unmistakably. He takes Ada's hand. Beat: resolution of the love arc.

chapters.title: The Essay I Meant to Write
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She rewrites the college essay — not about Cyrus, but about the version of herself who learned to stop being fine. She sends it to Cyrus first, then presses submit. Beat: authorship reclaimed.

chapters.title: Playlist, Continued
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Spring: acceptance letter, quiz bowl banquet where they're celebrated for second place, and a new shared playlist titled 'Volume Two.' Millbrook hasn't changed much — but Ada has stopped waiting for permission. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
